title: Exact point models and normalization of derived pullback composition
statement:
Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, the field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, and its fixed algebraic closure $k$, the datum of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Fix a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside the chosen algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma):s\to s$, where $\gamma=(z\mapsto z^q)^{-1}$ is geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. On the small pro-etale site of $s$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] use the constant ring sheaf $A_s$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], the category $D^b_c(s,A)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], and the point fiber functor $V=\operatorname{Fib}_s$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point].

Let $\mathcal M$ be the abelian category of $A_s$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $\mathcal D=D(\mathcal M)$, and $\mathsf L:\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal M)\to\mathcal D$ its localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $H_r=(h^r)^*$ for ordinary module pullback [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] with its canonical coefficient map [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], $Q_r=L(h^r)^*$ for derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], $\Gamma=\Gamma(s,-):\mathcal M\to A\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$ for final-object evaluation using constant scalars, with derived evaluation $V_{\mathrm{amb}}:\mathcal D\to D(A)$ induced by it [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], $C(F)$ for termwise application of a functor $F$, and $\mathsf L_A$ for localization of complexes of $A$-modules. Let $T_m:H_1H_m\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{m+1}$ be the ordinary canonical compositor. Let $t_m:Q_1Q_m\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{m+1}$ be the inverse of the prescribed derived composition isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition].

For every $r\geq1$, both $H_r$ and $\Gamma$ are exact, their termwise functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms, and the canonical exact-functor factorizations [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] identify $Q_r\mathsf L K$ with $\mathsf L C(H_r)K$ and derived evaluation $V_{\mathrm{amb}}\mathsf L K$ with $\mathsf L_A C(\Gamma)K$ for every complex $K$, without a K-flatness hypothesis on $K$. The functor $Q_r$ preserves $D^b_c(s,A)$; $V_{\mathrm{amb}}$ restricted there is precisely $V$. Under these factorizations and their iterated composition identifications, for every $m\geq1$ and every complex $K$,
$$t_{m,\mathsf L K}=\mathsf L\bigl(C(T_m)_K\bigr).$$
This equality uses the specified K-flat-normalized derived comparison, with the canonical constant-section coefficient maps on both sides.

For any natural transformation $\alpha:\Gamma\Rightarrow\Gamma H_r$ of $A$-module-valued functors on $\mathcal M$, the classes of its degreewise chain maps, through the displayed factorizations, define a unique natural transformation $\alpha^D:V_{\mathrm{amb}}\Rightarrow V_{\mathrm{amb}}Q_r$ on all of $\mathcal D$, with
$$\alpha^D_{\mathsf L K}=\mathsf L_A(C(\alpha)_K).$$
In particular its naturality holds for every derived morphism, including the inverse of every quasi-isomorphism. Equalities of chain maps built from these transformations and the ordinary $T_m$ remain equalities after localization with the specified $t_m$. These assertions restrict to the full subcategory $D^b_c(s,A)$.

proof.text: For every $r\geq1$, apply [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] to $u=h^r$ and the finite commutative coefficient ring $A$. Its scalar-transport functor is naturally the ordinary tensor module pullback $H_r$, so $H_r$ is exact. Apply [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] with $\mathcal A=A_s$: final-object evaluation is exact to $\Gamma(s,A_s)$-modules. Restricting scalars along the constant-section map $A\to\Gamma(s,A_s)$ leaves underlying abelian groups and kernels and cokernels unchanged, so the stated $A$-module-valued functor $\Gamma$ is exact as well. This does not assert that all sheaves on the pro-etale point are constant.

source.place: Tags 0982 and 098H (exact point sections); constant-coefficient module inverse image, with the scalar transport of prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to $H_r$ and to $\Gamma$. This gives quasi-isomorphism preservation and the natural exact-functor factorization isomorphisms on every cochain complex. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] the induced functor for $H_r$ is its total left derived functor, with its comparison to the ordinary termwise functor; thus it identifies with the specified $Q_r$ of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Denote the resulting comparison by $e_{r,K}:Q_r\mathsf LK\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathsf LC(H_r)K$ and the evaluation comparison by $v_K:V_{\mathrm{amb}}\mathsf LK\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathsf L_AC(\Gamma)K$. These are the canonical comparisons, not arbitrary isomorphisms of the representing objects. Every $K$ computes these functors; in particular these identifications restrict to their usual K-flat computations.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-constant-coefficient-composition] for the composable maps $h$ and $h^m$. Its equality $c_{h^m\circ h}=c_h\circ h^{-1}(c_{h^m})\circ\alpha_{h,h^m,A_s}$ shows that the ring map for $h^{m+1}$ is exactly the composite ring map required by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. The ordinary comparison of [lem-pur-proetale-module-pullback-composition] has direction $H_{m+1}\to H_1H_m$; its inverse is the $T_m$ in the statement. Consequently the ordinary and derived comparisons being compared use the same actual constant-section maps, rather than merely isomorphic coefficient sheaves.

proof.text: Fix $m\geq1$ and an arbitrary complex $K$. Choose $u:P\to K$ as in [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], so $P$ is K-flat with flat terms and $u$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The K-flat normalization in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], applied with first map $h$ and second map $h^m$, says that $c_{h,h^m,\mathsf LP}$ is the class of the ordinary comparison $H_{m+1}P\to H_1H_mP$. Taking inverses and using Step 2 identifies $t_{m,\mathsf LP}$ with $\mathsf L(C(T_m)_P)$. The cited composition statement includes that $H_mP$ is again K-flat with flat terms, so this computes the iterated derived pullback as well. The resolution is taken in all module sheaves; neither its terms nor $P$ are required to be bounded or constructible.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution) and 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition), including its use of pullback of K-flat complexes

proof.text: Write $A_K=\mathsf LC(H_1)C(H_m)K$ and $B_K=\mathsf LC(H_{m+1})K$, and let $\widetilde t_K:A_K\to B_K$ be $t_{m,\mathsf LK}$ conjugated by the iterated comparisons $e$ of Step 2. Put $b_K=\mathsf L(C(T_m)_K)$, $a=\mathsf LC(H_1)C(H_m)(u)$ and $b=\mathsf LC(H_{m+1})(u)$. Naturality of $t_m$ and of $e$ gives $\widetilde t_K\circ a=b\circ\widetilde t_P$; ordinary naturality of $T_m$ gives $b_K\circ a=b\circ b_P$. Step 4 says $\widetilde t_P=b_P$, while Step 2 makes $a$ invertible. Cancelling $a$ gives $\widetilde t_K=b_K$, precisely the required equality on every representative. This is a cancellation of two naturality squares and introduces no new comparison theorem.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; elementary naturality and cancellation extending its K-flat computation

proof.text: The map $h^r$ is a scheme isomorphism: its inverse is induced by $\gamma^{-r}$, with $\gamma$ as in [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. For a complex whose class belongs to $D^b_c(s,A)$, [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback] therefore gives that its $Q_r$-image also belongs to $D^b_c(s,A)$. Here $\ell\ne p$ ensures that $\ell$ is invertible on $s$, and $n\geq1$ is exactly the finite-coefficient case of that lemma. Part 1 of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] defines $V$ by these same termwise final-object sections; [lem-weil-point-sections-finiteness] (1) ensures that they land in $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$. Hence restriction of $V_{\mathrm{amb}}$ is the stated $V$, with the target viewed inside $D(A)$. This is a restriction of the ambient evaluation already constructed, rather than a separate choice of a fiber functor.

source.place: Finite-level point evaluation clause; isomorphism pullback identification in lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback

proof.text: Let $\alpha:\Gamma\Rightarrow\Gamma H_r$ be as in the statement. Naturality for each differential $d_K^i$ gives $\Gamma H_r(d_K^i)\alpha_{K^i}=\alpha_{K^{i+1}}\Gamma(d_K^i)$, so its degreewise components form a chain map $C(\alpha)_K:C(\Gamma)K\to C(\Gamma)C(H_r)K$. For a chain map $f:K\to K'$, degreewise naturality similarly gives $C(\Gamma)C(H_r)(f)\circ C(\alpha)_K=C(\alpha)_{K'}\circ C(\Gamma)(f)$. Thus localization in $A$-modules gives a natural transformation between the two functors on complexes. No additivity in the variable $K$ is required of the family $\alpha$ beyond its given $A$-linear components and naturality.

source.place: Tag 04VG, lemma-properties-left-localization, input natural transformation; elementary degreewise chain-map verification

proof.text:
Both $F_1=\mathsf L_AC(\Gamma)$ and $F_2=\mathsf L_AC(\Gamma)C(H_r)$ invert quasi-isomorphisms by Step 2. Their chosen factorizations through $\mathsf L$ are $V_{\mathrm{amb}}$ and $V_{\mathrm{amb}}Q_r$. More explicitly set $w_K=v_{C(H_r)K}\circ V_{\mathrm{amb}}(e_{r,K})$. Apply part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to the natural transformation $\tau_K=\mathsf L_A(C(\alpha)_K)$ constructed in Step 7. It supplies the unique natural transformation on all of $\mathcal D$ whose component is
$$\alpha^D_{\mathsf LK}=w_K^{-1}\circ\tau_K\circ v_K.$$
Under the displayed factorizations this is exactly the component formula in the statement. Full faithfulness in the cited localization result gives uniqueness among all derived natural transformations with those components, including when $\alpha$ is not an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 04VG, lemma-properties-left-localization; natural-transformation enhancement: Mathlib CategoryTheory/Localization/Predicate.lean, fullyFaithfulWhiskeringLeft and liftNatTrans (lines 278 and 326)

proof.text: For any derived morphism $f:X\to Y$, Step 8 gives $(V_{\mathrm{amb}}Q_r)(f)\alpha^D_X=\alpha^D_YV_{\mathrm{amb}}(f)$. If $f=\mathsf L(u)$ for a quasi-isomorphism, multiply this equality on the left by $(V_{\mathrm{amb}}Q_r)(f)^{-1}$ and on the right by $V_{\mathrm{amb}}(f)^{-1}$ to obtain naturality for $f^{-1}$. Localization is a functor, so it preserves equalities, identities and compositions of chain maps. By Steps 5 and 8 their localized factors are exactly the specified $t_m$ and $\alpha^D$, after conjugating by the specified factorization isomorphisms; intermediate factorization maps and their inverses cancel in a composite. If such an identity is expressed as an identity of natural transformations, part (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] detects it on all $\mathsf LK$. Finally, Step 6 permits restriction of these functors and transformations to the full subcategory $D^b_c(s,A)$; fullness retains naturality for every morphism there.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q63-ec9dbe8de (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read all nine steps and every cited statement. The statement is byte-identical to the live node. The only stmt_dep added is lem-pur-proetale-module-pullback-composition, which supplies the compositor T_m that the statement uses. There are no new nodes. The item is still unsplit live, with no repair note, so it is not superseded and not a re-split. No SGA source is used. Step 1: prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact (any morphism, finite ring) plus lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact (k algebraically closed) give exactness, with restriction of scalars exact. Step 2: exact-functor factorization plus the derived-functor (Kan extension) node match the K-flat Q_r of def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom. Step 3: lem-trf-constant-coefficient-composition with k=h^m gives exactly the composite ring identification that the derived-composition lemma requires; the direction of the lem-pur compositor (H_{m+1}->H_1H_m) was checked, and T_m is its inverse. Step 4: K-flat flat-term resolution (lem-pc-kflat-resolution), with c_{h,h^m} equal to the termwise class, as in Stacks 0D6D l.3658-3681. Step 5: I rechecked the two naturality squares and the cancellation of the invertible a; it is valid for unbounded, non-K-flat K. Step 6: h^r is an isomorphism, and lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback (ell invertible since ell!=p, n>=1) gives D^b_c preservation; Fib_s clause 1 and point-sections-finiteness (1) give V_amb|D^b_c = V. Steps 7-9: chain maps from naturality, then localization universal property parts (2) and (3), with phi_2 = v∘V(e). This gives a unique alpha^D with the stated components, with no invertibility assumption on alpha. Stacks tags 0D6D/06YS/06YY/015F/03D8/03CB/0H7J/04VG/0982/098H resolve to the named labels. The blueprint 'transports the pair' paragraph exists in the main-20261015 compact-description proof. Edge cases checked: alpha=0, m=1, K=0, n>1. The generic tool_uses are accepted. Minor, no change: Step 9 is marked elementary while citing localization (2)/(3).
